analysis.name: Amanda Cass
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 43 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: The lectures are so engaging and fun. Cass makes the material super simple and easy to understand. I barely had to study for this class but I can understand how some of the concepts can be difficult to grasp as there are many small parts to certain mechanisms. If you can do all homework/quiz questions and review slides you will be great on exams.

Lectures are very material heavy, but that is expected in a biology course. Everything on the exams are given to you in the slides. As long as you attend class and review the slides you will fly by with an A. Attendance is mandatory through an iClicker you need to purchase. All in all, probably the best science teacher I've ever had!!

Great professor. I didn't have to study for any tests because all the lectures had easily digestible information that stacked on top of each other. No complaints except for the TAs, they were all snobs who never could accept being wrong

Pretty solid professor. The lab was straightforward and I was personally blessed with a good lab partner, making it a nice lab in general. It's a smaller class so she is easily accessible, not to mention the other professors who are lab assistants and the TAs who can help you throughout the lab. Cool project in the end where you DNA swab your dog.

Amazing professor, couldn't have asked for a better professor. She's very easy and tries to make the class fun, as it may be a gen-ed for some people. Slides are very easy to understand, and the talking pace is slow so that we can take notes during the class. The exams aren't hard at all if you put in the work and study!

analysis.name: Alexandra Jesse
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 53 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: DO NOT TAKE THIS CLASS. unless this class is needed for your major I wouldn't take it. 80% of the final grade is exams (4 exams, 1 final), she records lectures but you can't access it unless you have an excused absence (like being sick), and she talks really soft so you can't hear her well. she's sweet as a person but not the greatest professorl

Really boring class and lectures are really dry. You have to pay very good attention in class and when reading the book if you want to do well. Crutches are there to help (drop the lowest test grade.. etc) but still tests and in class writing assignments are really tough. Definitely need to drop the lowest grades and do all SONA extra credit.

Avoid this prof is possible! Writes her own exams (1st language isn't english), so some questions are confusing. Attendance is mandatory, only get 2 absences. After 1st exam every ~5th class is another exam. Doesn't show final grade on canvas, so no idea how screwed I am. Nice person but not good prof. Avoid, avoid, avoid!!!!

Has 4 exams, including final, drops one of three lowest exams all graded 20% of your grade. If you honestly do well in the first 3 you dont have to worry too much on the final since they are all graded the same. Loved her little accent especially when she says PLUE instead of BLUE. You will do fine if you are passionate about the subject.

I loved Professor Jesse's class. If you go to class and take notes the exams are very easy. Most of the people I'd heard in class complaining that she was difficult to hear are the same people who would spend all of class talking or on their phones. She also gives study guides that are very good exam prep. Over all good teacher and I learned a lot

analysis.name: Craig Albertson
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Honestly disagree with his ratings. He is a nice guy, content is hard but it's a 582 level class what do u expect. He provided study guides that were nearly identical to exam so it's 100% manageable despite being open response if you just study that. I find the reading quizzes to be harder than exams. Lab fairly easy. Great lecturer imo
He actually teaches like a normal person idk how to explain it but he swears so much and is so real in the best way possible. Hard class but the way he teaches it is great

This class was a lot more challenging this expected. There was so much information to memorize and just the overall content was not what I was looking forward to. Exams were hard overall and required a lot of studying. Some cool topics and really nice professor maybe just was not for me.
Just don't take any of his classes, does not know how to communicate and his exams and grading are just ridiculous, wouldn't recommend
Same guy here. Also took a picture with him and his fish tanks. 10/10 experience.

analysis.name: Lori Astheimer Best
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 158 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Honestly just a really great professor. Very clear and informative lectures. Its clear she cares about her students doing well. It is a very content heavy class with very difficult concepts. Also exam heavy, 5 midterms, optional final. Although this class was hard Dr. A had lots of extra credit, and lots of help opportunities.

there are not a lot of assignments to help you if you dont do well on the 5 exams we have. she talks so fast, the only plus is that you can do the class on zoom. The exams were kinda hard and i would not recommending taking this if you are a normal psych student.

Truly the best professor I've ever been blessed to have. PLEASE attend the most lectures you can because they are the most comprehensive and engaging hours of my college experience so far. She has so much extra credit that it is hard to not get an A in this class. Attendance is through TopHat and you can join from zoom if needed, but go in person!!

She is amazing. Dr. A offers a zoom link to watch class live while not attending in person. Quizzes are take home and multiple choice. She is very passionate about neuroscience. The class is very big but she does encourage participation and talking with people near you. She is amazing, even if science is not your thing you can do great.

Dr. A explains the material clearly and makes sure to clarify anything people ask about. She encourages questions and answers in easy to understand ways. Assignments: weekly 15 min or less surveys and one final project.

analysis.name: Annie Raymond
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: If you come into uni with no previous calc experience (like I did) youre cooked. Certain concepts just dont get explained and you have to self-teach no matter how many lectures you show up to. She'd teach for the entire 50-minute lecture and I'd walk out feeling like I knew less and less every time. Easy to cheat on hw and quizzes to save ur grade!

The average was low, but I I think she is very intelligent, inspirational, and willing to explain any concept to you. It was a short class and the course chair controlled most everything in terms of grading, material, and deadlines. She taught very fast, so prep before, ask ?'s, and do practice exams!!

Lectures often made simple concepts confusing, and I rarely left class with clarity. Exam averages were low, there is no curve, and handwriting made notes hard to follow. I taught myself most material, making this class tough on your GPA. DO NOT TAKE!

Worst professor Ive had. Did not learn anything from her and had to do everything on my own. You will get caught off guard during exam, and she makes simple things seem extremely complex. Seems nice, but honestly does not outweigh the horrors of this class. There is no curving in this class, and no leniency with missed assignments. DO NOT TAKE!!!

Raymond was a by far the best professor available for 127, however the class was horrendous and she failed to explain the content clearly. You NEED to study- homework, lectures, and exams barely relate. To her benefit, her practice exams are the best across the course and the Course Chair is at fault for most issues.

analysis.name: Soroosh Azizi
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 44 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: People are just mad because a class got to take a test online because canvas was all messed up for an hour. Isenberg honestly just gives kids the mentality that everything is an easy A... this school a joke. Study for your test next time pal instead of moaning and yelling.  Hate isn't fully deserved let the guy not stress because you can't study

He always prepares a study guide with everything you need to know before the exam and videos on how to complete the HWs step by step. Exams are all multiple choice online and the answers are not there to trick you. Very straight forward and to the point. Entertaining in class and cares about his students participating.

Might be the worst professor. Soroosh has no business teaching an online class, or teaching a course in general. He should consider any other profession regarding finance because he doesn't teach or know how to properly. He has very strict grading policies with few assignments. If you mess up on one exam there is pretty much no coming back from it.

Expects students to perform excel formulas using a financial calculator for In-person exams (1 MINUTE) per question. No time to double check your work even if you finish each question within that minute. And if you don't have a financial calculator, good luck! Double sided cheat sheets are allowed, best of luck fitting 50 pages of exam material in!

Funniest professor I have ever had which keeps the lectures super engaging. Even at 8am he always comes with great energy, and he is clearly passionate about what he teaches. He is strict about due dates and struggled a bit figuring out how to administer exams since it was his first semester @UM. Cant rec Azizi enough, will seek for future courses.

analysis.name: Andrew Havens
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 108 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: If your shaky on calc or math in general Havens will not help you. Left each class not really learning too much and going to the SI sessions became part of my schedule. He just reads off the slides and expects you to absorb the information and his explanations were no help. Considered not going to classes many times--> Went anyways--> Regretted it.

Epitome of evil.average grade on both exams were in the 59-65 range, and instead of offering help or extra credit for struggling students, his advice for them was to drop the class, it's pretty apparent he takes pride in students struggling. If you have taken calc before, i'd advise you to stay out of lecture and learn the material on your own.

Hated this class. He overcomplicated topics that couldve been explained more simply. He is also lowkey rude to students. If you didnt take calc in high school DO NOT TAKE IT WITH HAVENS. Now I have to retake it because I bombed the midterm, and there was no coming back from it. If you didn't hear me clearly the first time, do not take this class.

If you enjoy life to any sort of degree, do not take 127 with this professor. Besides the fact that he explains arbitrarily easy concepts using graduate material, making them far more complicated than need be, he just genuinely sucks at actually making sure his students understand the material. I suggest going to a different professor's lecture.

He often laughed at students for answering incorrectly, creating an uncomfortable environment. While homework and quizzes were conducted online (two per week), the final exams were in person. Don't recommend raising your hand in class because even if you get it right, he will undermine it and make it sound wrong. Overcomplicates everything.

analysis.name: Anita Milman
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment:
Lots of resources to read up on (often like 10+ pages).
Lectures are a little on the boring side but it's feasible to just be on your phone and look at the slides later.
Great professor :)

Professor Milman made this class interesting and fun. I looked forward to it. Group work, class, activities, and reading quizzes are the important chunk of your grade. I took the class as honors and the projects she had us do made us very passionate about the subject of environmental policy. This was a class every major should be required to take.

I had her for NRC 309. She did a great job at making our lectures not feel like lectures by making us get into discussions with small groups at our tables, sometimes doing mini projects. Homework was mainly just annotating and commenting on Perusall readings; tedious but pretty easy.  The course was somewhat difficult but expected for a 300 level.

Very enthusiastic and passionate about policy. 10 HW quizzes straight from textbook 3 exams (sorta hard especially the multiple choice parts) and class assignments done in table groups. Attendance is mandatory but never actually taken. Overall a pretty easy intro to environmental policy class-PS 1st month is just intro to policy.

this was a good class to take if you are interested in the workings of how policies are made! i loved that we got the option to actually experience "making laws" and used games to help our learning along. easy class; only two exams and most hw were reading assignments

analysis.name: Robert Bowse
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: His feedback is alright but he gives so much unnecessary busy work compared to other professors you can take. I would recommend someone else.

Professor Bowse is a good professor in a very useful class. No exams, just weekly assignments which make up for 80% of your grade. Class is pretty useful in getting you prepared for internships, as you work on resumes/cover letters. Some assignments are longer than others, but nothing too bad. Do the assignments and show up, and you will get an A.

Professor Bowse has quite a deceptive rating of 4.3. His grading is extremely picky and assignments must be completed HIS way or no way. In terms of workload, this Junior year writing class has considerably more work than other professors.

The class has WAYYYY too much work for a 1 credit course. To add insult to injury the work is graded obscenely harshly. If you are able to take this class with anyone else do it. In terms of how he actually is as a professor he's actually not bad, very clear and engaging, just assigns way too much work.

Class is insanely easy. Literally show up, do the homework and online quizzes, and you'll get an A. It's also incredibly helpful for building a great resume and making your LinkedIn professional. It's worth paying attention and putting effort in too, as most of the material is applicable to real life

analysis.name: Kathleen Brown-Perez
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 46 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Kathleen is literally one of the best professors I've ever had. To pass, all you really need to do is show up and participate in the discussions. She even bought our class donuts. I highly recommend her and respect her as a professor.

Great professor with a love for teaching and the course material. She was an excellent instructor to have for my first semester of college. Her course was mostly rooted in group discussion. One of the few instructors for 201H that does not require you to buy any materials. I wish I could have her again.

Kathleen is a great professor for Criminal Law. I took this class as an elective and was a little nervous about its difficulty going into it but as long as you care and are willing to put a little effort in, no one should have a problem getting a good grade. This class is at 8:30 and I have no problem getting up for it because its so interesting!

I think her classes are very chill and enjoyable. The content of this course is helpful beyond college life, and she's a nice professor, too. I'd recommend reading the material (she doesn't assign much) and trying to participate in class discussions. Fair grading with clear criteria, you will do well as long as you care.

If you can, take her class for Ideas that Change the World! It's almost completely discussion-based, so attendance and participation are critical. There are 3 graded reflection essays that are super manageable. Getting an A is easy if you just attend class.

analysis.name: Erin Baker
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 26 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Requires attendance and will call you out for being on your phone / laptop. Lectures have almost nothing to do with climate engineering and are structured like primary school class. Class is entirely a waste of time, this professor should not be teaching engineering at UMass. Guest speaker accomplished more in one lecture than she has in weeks.

ENGIN 113? More like HIPPIE 101. Learned more about sustainability than I did engineering.  No need to even take notes or pay attention in class.  The lab is what I looked forward to the most, even though you teach yourself how to use desigining software.  Creo 2.0 is a must have for this class, since you'll be learning straight from the book

In class she mostly does practice problems that you are put into groups for, as long as you vaguely understood the reading they are not super hard. There is Iclicker attendance so attendance is mandatory. Homework is light apart from the readings that are occasionally extremely long. Exams are not a lot of questions but are open note and open book.

Extremely boring class. Has nothing to do with learning mechanical engineering. Learn more about economics than anything. Pretty much learn what you could easily learn in one day over the entire semester. Lots of guest speakers. No midterm or final and the quizzes are open note.  Project required that's worked on all semester.
Class was mad easy once you get the hang of excel

analysis.name: Eric Sarfo Amponsah
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 178 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Completely unable to maintain interest in class or explain things. Sets literally impossible quiz times, enforces them with a rigidity that suggests he mostly loves a power trip. Regularly takes days to respond to emails. Has difficulty answering student questions clearly. Sets unclear standards for grading tests and enforces them rigidly

This professor does not care about people in extenuating situations. I tried to get help from him but he rejected every request from me. All other professors offered help and weight adjustment to give me a chance to pass the course. He is the worst professor I have ever met this semester.
He's quite condescending, and also automatically assumes students just want to cheat and get away with things. That will be his default perception if you ask him about anything.

If you have no external issues, no disabilities, then you're fine taking this prof. If you do, then avoid him. Even if you are registered with disability services/ Dean of Students, he won't work with you. He might not even believe you.
If he's your only option, and you're having trouble, you're better off not approaching him and just try to pass.

You will learn nothing from taking Math235 with Eric. I repeat, NOTHING! He weaponizes exams instead of using them to test understanding, and his poor attitude towards teaching is already palpable from the start. Even if you do well, you'll walk away feeling worn out. This guy does NOT deserve a paycheck as he thinks students are beneath him.

analysis.name: Brokk Toggerson
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 130 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Grading is fuzzy. Nothing is clear cut, and doesn't clarify if you ask about it. He's rude when communicating. He's one of those professors that the subject makes so much sense to him that he can't understand why it doesn't make sense to you. Classwork is easy, but exams are difficult and near impossible.

Showing up and filling in a scantron was 30% of the final grade. Literally just put down your name, SID, and a few bubbled answers and sneak out.  He tries really hard and believes in the power of TBL but it sucks ass. HW, lab, AND test material are not covered in class because he takes all class to explain 1 problem. Gotta learn on your own.

I have always disliked physics. I was very confused the whole semester. This is the lowest level physics class offered (I believe) and was not that easy. It was a "teach yourself ahead of lecture" type class and team based learning. I hope they improve the class structure. Only did well because participation grade was contributed GREATLY.

Does not teach. Literally, you are expected to just read the book and there is no lecture whatsoever. Want to take physics with Toggerson? You're better off just buying a book and teaching yourself than paying $20k to have a professor tell you to read a book and teach yourself. Thanks UMass. I got to teach myself physics.

Brokk is nice. His teaching style, however, is harrowing. Studying for his violating 7 question exams is hell because he tries to reinvent the wheel with the way he teaches you normally stupidly easy physics concepts. The cherry on top is that I can't even find external resources to supplement literally anything Brokk taught in class. What a joke.

analysis.name: Hendrik Van den Berg
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 70 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: He failed half of the 200 person lecture on the first midterm. He goes off on tangents in lecture and isn't straightforward with information that we need to know for the exams, but instead likes to spew his extremely liberal idealogy that is irrelevant. He also assigns very long readings, but no powerpoints to help supplement the readings.

Compiles extremely fascinating content pertaining to the course. Knowledgeable about history, politics, and of course, econ and creation of economic models. Assignments are short and just check you pay attention in lecture and do some of the readings. Accessible outside of class and not hard to talk to. Could listen to his lectures for hours.

He's definitely a tough grader. He often goes on tangents about his time in Brazil and throws the class off course. About 20% of the things he says are actually important (and you'll miss them if you don't pay attention). Studied for 2 hours off of YouTube tutorials for his final and learned the same material that he took 6 weeks to explain.

The class is graded pretty much on 2 things only (the midterm and final). The exams are open notes (handwritten only) and they are open ended. If you can show that you did the readings, you'll do good. He is a very intelligent and kind person. He takes attendance and forbids any electronics. Overall, would take again.

All throughout the semester you thought you were going to do well because the TA graded the homework. He grades the exams himself and failed nearly everyone. Do not take any class with him. This is the most absurdly graded course I have taken in my 3 years of college.

analysis.name: Joseph Bergan
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: I enjoyed how he used personal research experiences to explain different concepts in the class. Attendance is mandatory, and lectures can be slow at some points, but overall, they are very engaging. Didn't do well on the first two exams, but once I understood the format of the exams, I scored a lot better. Would recommend!
Reason I pursued neuroscience. If you have even a passing interest in neuroscience then you must take this class. If you believe the lectures are boring then you should ask questions, engage.

I really enjoyed this class! Prof Bergan is a super knowledgeable person with a lot of fascinating insights into neuroscience related things, so I'd encourage reaching out to him outside of class. Lectures are important, as his slides don't have everything written out. Grading on reaction papers is a little unclear though.

Bergan is knowledgable and understanding. If you are interested in neuroscience research, he is a good person to talk to. As a lecturer, he can be boring with no clickers or group work, making it hard to take notes and remain engaged. His slides don't really have words on them and there is so much content. But, exams and papers are relatively easy.

If you're interested in neuroscience, he is the professor to take. However, the class is lecture-heavy, and there is not a lot of room for participation. There is no homework, but there are weekly quizzes, four reaction papers to readings, and one final paper. For the exams, they are lecture-heavy which can sometimes be hard to pay attention for.

analysis.name: Kathleen Brown
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Kathleen runs one of the easiest classes you will take, but there were times when she gave blatantly false or outdated information, and if you have a background in the social sciences, you may notice how she butchers some topics and misses a lot of nuance. I'd love to take her class on American Indian Law, but 201H with her was unfulfilling.
Great professor. She provides all material needed for finishing reading. She is also very kind and caring plus nonchalant.

Kathleen is LITERALLY the BEST professor you will ever find at UMass!!!! She understands that this class isn't meant to dominate your life and so she keeps it fairly simple and gives clear instructions. And everyday at the end of class she offers you help and to go to her office with her. She also gives some extra credit assignments during semester

Class=mandatory, but get out early some days.  The books are interesting and as long as you're trying, shell help you. DO NOT fall asleep or be late.  BUY the MLA handbook and bring it to class. Shes very proud of being native american so dont her started on how the world has tortured her people. Thinks shes the greatest, but its funny so its okay.

I loved Kathleen's class. I strongly feel like an honors requirement like 291A should supplement the curriculum, not overtake your semester, and Kathleen did a great job with it. The reading was light; we had no essays and only one project. You don't have to buy the books; she provides the passages online. Would recommend her for this class.

analysis.name: Cruz Davis
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 19 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: The entire semester, he did not reply to any email I ever sent him. Gets very frustrated when you don't understand the content and often refuses to further explain because we "should just know this by now". Is always 10+ minutes late to class. Understandable to think this will be an "Easy A" gen ed. IT. WILL. NOT.

He changed the entire curriculum from medical ethics to philosophy of medicine because he was too embarrassed to talk about abortion and pregnancy. He gives heavy lectures and grades each student very differently. He also changed student's grades on assignments at the very last minute before grades were due. DO NOT take his class, RUN.

He doesn't have slides for the class and doesn't post anything on canvas besides readings so you have to be in class. He does not follow his own syllabus and says he can change your grade by any percentage he feels based off your effort and participation. It doesn't feel like he knows what hes talking about half of the time. I would NEVER suggest!

This class gave difficult papers that took longer to understand the language than understand the piece. Prof didn't like questions and had a hard time helping when confused which was often. He required office hours and had a lot of group projects which were difficult when a solid amount of people in the class didn't understand. Decent lecturer tho.

Showed up late almost every day. He sent emails with required work at 3 in the morning, due in a day, then didn't understand why people were confused with his unclear instructions. Never made it clear what we were supposed to be doing in or out of class; majority of class was confused all of the time. Rude to students and makes inappropriate jokes.

analysis.name: Chul Park
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I had to withdraw from this class. Mandatory attendance and 2% off your total grade every time you missed no matter what. There was no homework which was a pro and con. The con being the class was very exam heavy. The average on the first exam was a 50% and the second exam was the on the Monday right after Spring Break. Noted slides are not posted.

Professor Park does not upload his annotated notes online for review. No homework is assigned, which sounds nice, but exams are very heavily factored into your overall grade. Exams are also difficult, with the average on the first exam being 50. Attendance is also mandatory, and almost 2% of your grade is lost just for missing a class each time.

Not a lot of homework but lab assignments are long and difficult. He is lecture heavy and attendance isn't mandatory but he doesn't upload annotated notes. He is a poor lecturer and takes a long time to answer emails. He doesn't provide much to prepare for exams. Nice guy but bad professor. Don't expect much help or sympathy.

Overall layout of the class was very disorganized and confusing. We never finished the curriculum set out in the syllabus and topics covered were disproportionally covered on the exams. No HW so the exams are everything and Park gives little to no insight or guidance on how to prepare for exams. Non-responsive to emails. Grading is pretty lenient.

He likes to teach with an overhead projector with handouts/packets that you fill in as each lecture progresses. Lectures are late during the day on TuTh. Homeworks are relatively straightforward and simple if you put in some thoughts and the exams are a little more difficult but that is to be expected. He takes attendance so don't skip.

analysis.name: Garrett Cahill
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 71 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Took over the summer. Very clear criteria listed in the syllabus. It's easy to pick yourself back up after falling behind, but you should still stay on track. Please don't cheat, just pay attention so you can learn the material normally. Trust me, your experience will be much smoother that way. Effort is required.

Took asynchronously. Great prerecorded lectures, as well as TA and prof office hours. Written homework and practice exams reflect exams perfectly, no surprises in this class. Concepts can be tricky to grasp, but there is a lot of good info provided in textbooks and lectures. My only complaint is how long it took for written homework to be graded.

I didn't even have him as a professor, and I still went to his lectures because he really is *that good*. Super accessible outside of class and clearly cares about student success. Super enthusiastic and easy to follow, and really good about clearing up points of confusion. Don't take MATH 331 with anyone else but Garrett.
Super caring and accessible outside of class. Took the time to get to know everyone's names. This class wasn't super challenging, but he explained concepts very clearly. Simply the GOAT.

Garrett makes complicated material straightforward and takes care to get to know his students. He made calc 3 approachable and broke the content down so it was easy to follow. I really enjoyed his class and got a lot out of it. Would recommend as I believe he is one of the best math professors I have had.

analysis.name: Jeffrey Beaulieu
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 260 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: Two exams and a final. Weekly homework, graded tough. Go to class and discussion and get 6 points on your average. GO TO OFFICE HOURS!!! it's easy if you get help. He's really nice and tries to be clear. Discussion is optional but helpful. Tests are straightforward, offers review sessions that are extremely helpful! Not a bad class if you try hard!

I am a d1 Jeff glazer. I suck at math and this guy was so helpful when instructing as he focused on the why we do things instead of just doing it. As an extra plus, I love his voice he sounds like Obama. Homework is super easy but MyMathLab is expensive and sucks as a program. Jeff I love you I wish I could take you to Math 127 with me.

This is the only math class I have ever felt confident in. HIGHLY recommend Jeff.
All homework assignments will be on Pearson's My Math Lab. This will give you the opportunity to try problems multiple times and find study materials on what you struggle with. Each class is recorded and uploaded to Canvas in Echo360.

Jeff is such a nice guy and he explains most topics well. All exams are multiple choice and typically no more than 20 questions, 5 being free points! Attendance is not mandatory and lectures are recorded, but he looks sad if you don't come to class :( so go to class for king Jeff we love him

I've NEVER succeeded in math until having Jeff as a professor. He explains everything so simply, and his tests are beyond doable. Not to mention he's so kind and wholesome. As a sophomore, he's honestly my favorite professor thus far! I genuinely have nothing negative to say about him or his class.

analysis.name: Yossi Chait

Be ready for the quizzes and exams. It just a midterm and a final. be sure to take GREAT notes during lecture because the quizzes and exams are very specific. You get a cheat sheet so make sure to put as much as you can. Extra credits are VERY helpful so make sure to do the required assignments. 1 group project, read directions carefully.
I used to not wear my seatbelt when driving to class in hopes I wouldn't make it there.

Worst Professor I've ever had. He makes the quizzes and exams so particular and detailed that you look at the paper and say "what am I even looking at." You have so much material to study for yet he chooses the smallest and most random things to test you on

Professor Fiocchi is a great guy and does seem to care about his students. For some reason though, I am always confused when doing the assignments and exams. Maybe I don't pay enough attention in the lectures but it never seems like I learn much. It might just be me but I've taken 3 classes with Professor Fiocchi and everytime I've struggled. Tough

analysis.name: Robert Feingold
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 27 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: One of the best professors I had in college. He has the most real world experience of any of the finance professors and it really shows. In terms of work, you will have a couple of projects, a midterm, and final. He clearly outlines what he wants and how to do it. Personally, I did not find this class to be very hard, but I know a few who did.

He is indeed one of the best professors I took. He really cares about his students' improvement in future career. The exam is pretty hard but straightforward but if you pay attention in class you will be fine. There are no recorded lectures and slides are mostly companies' data since it only understandable during lectures. He deserves 5s rating.

Robert Feingold is hands down the best professor I've had through my college career. The topic itself is challenging, but he does a great job breaking down what you need to know. I can't say enough good about him, easy grader, funny guy, easily accessible when you need help, and a caring professor who wants to see his students do well. Love him!

This was a great class to take and Prof. Feingold clearly cares about his students. Exams were hard, but if you genuinely pay attention in class and properly study they will come easy to you. The homework  were relatively straightforward. Group project was not too bad as long as you communicate well with your group.

Robert is a great professor. His class is hard, but he does his best to help you succeed. He gives a decent amount of HW, but its not too difficult and most of it prepares you for real-world work you'll do in the office. His lectures are great. He is entertaining, funny, and gives real world stories from his experiences. His ratings make sense here

analysis.name: Faruk Akkus
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He tries his best and he's nice, but syntax is very difficult and I think he struggles to explain it sometimes. If you miss a single class, you MUST rewatch the lectures to catch up. It's not a lot of work, but it's a very challenging class and he grades quite harshly sometimes. He's very nice, though, and willing to help those in need.

Took his LING 201 class. Prof. Faruk plans his lectures very well, and uses class time effectively. As long as you show up to lectures, you'll do fine. He makes sure students understand the class material really solidly, but won't elaborate beyond the scope of the course. However, this keeps class on-topic and on track.

Great class! Explains the subject matter clearly & is enthusiastic about it too. Communicates well w/ the class & is a good person in general! There's a section where (as it's a gen ed class) we go over the IPA, so if u're alr a LING major & took 201 prior to this, that part'll be pretty easy. If u need to fulfill your HIS gen ed, take this class!

Professor Akkus is very good at explaining difficult concepts. His syntax class is very informative, and I appreciated the detailed explanations on the slides. It is important to show up to lectures, since he moves quickly through the material. Office hours were at accessible times, as were the TA's.
Fantastic at Explaining Concepts. Would take him many times more. This is from 150 Ling not 401 though. It did not give me the option to chose this class.

analysis.name: Steve Fox
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Fox was far and away the best professor I had in my freshman year at UMass, he was funny, knowledgeable, engaging, and you got the sense that he really cared about his field and his students. Take this class if you get the chance, even if you are not studying or interested in journalism directly.

Most of the class is pretty straightforward and not terribly difficult. He's a pretty lenient grader and papers aren't terribly long, plus Bull Quizzes (textbook) and midterm is open note. However, the news quizzes were the only hard part as questions range from local national and international news. Theyre either general or very specific questions

News Quizzes can be tough at times, sometimes having rather obscure topics. His lectures are fairly engaging with many real-world examples, and while the discussions can drag a bit, they often do address important topics. The papers are usually fairly straight-forward, with most being a minimum of 500 words. Took for a gen-ed, would recommend.

The class started out with a clear goal in mind. However, as the semester progressed the expectations and the requirements were kind of thrown out the window. I felt that Fox checked out mentally mid way through the semester and didn't really care to give helpful feedback on the majority of work. He makes you question the value of your education.

Took Sports in Film, Literature and Journalism with him. Not my first class with Fox and have always enjoyed them. Aside from a few papers and books to read, the work is not too intense in this class, and he's always flexible about due dates and willing to cooperate with students. Class is heavy on discussions.

analysis.name: Z Fareen Parvez
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I thought theory was gonna be awful, but Professor Parvez actually makes the tough language very accessible and interesting (and actually somewhat easy?). I really enjoy this class and she's a great lecturer. 2 giant take-home exams, 2 smaller papers, and discussion section.

this class was a ton of work (especially the last few weeks) with lots of reading. I didn't read everything but it would definitely have helped for the take-home tests. Lectures are also super helpful because the readings are really dense but she does a really good job of breaking it all down. Also, you can find most of the readings online for free

I've tried to take theory twice before and dropped it both times because I hated it. Fareen keeps it interesting and the class isn't too difficult. There are 2 take home exams and a few smaller papers but none of them are too difficult. Discussion attendance is mandatory, lecture isn't, but if you don't do the readings, lecture really helps.

I didn't mind the actual content of this course, for the most part, it was more of how the class was taught and the assignments that made it hard. She doesn't take attendance, if you miss one class you will be completely lost and the end of the semester is PACKED with assignments that pile up on each other near finals, making it really stressful.

analysis.name: Arturo Figliola
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 29 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Absolutely amazing!!! He says hi outside of class, responds to my emails, is very easy to reach and dedicated to helping all of his students. He's genuinely so kind and funny, he makes Italian fun. He teaches by barely speaking English in class, but won't hesitate to clarify. Can't wait to spend the next few years getting my BA with Italian.
Great guy, you have to participate in the class and will definitely learn if you give the effort. Wouldn't call the class easy but studying for the class at least for me was enjoyable.
Professor Figliola is great! He's kind, funny and has an engaging teaching style. I learned so much from this course and genuinely enjoyed going.

Arturo is the best teacher in the Italian department.  It's a shame, though, that he doesn't teach any upper-level courses but 303.  He was amazing.  He explains things in Italian until you understand.  I wish I could have taken him more than once.  He's also nice and hilarious.  Yay Arturo!!!

Here is the truth about this guy: He is charming and funny but he does not have a good teaching method. Very few students can learn from his "emersion method"(no english in the class). It seems like he writes the tests last minute (his reviews are a joke). Dont take this class unless you already have a good understanding of the italian lang.

analysis.name: Forrest Bowlick
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 12 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: He's a nice guy with a well-structured class. Our assignments are GIS labs where we have multiple TAs to help us. You can turn in things late with no grade-related penalty (not turning in an assignment will block you from accessing the next module, however). Fun final project which is a poster you present at a symposium. Has a snack box in lab.

This class was great - pretty much all of the work for it and most of the learning gets done in lab time which is really well structured and you always have the TAs and Forrest there to help. He's a super fun and caring guy who I'd definitely recommend taking a class with.

Love Forrest, he's really understanding and helpful. I really did not understand GIS but he helps you through it. Lectures are not really important, just have to go to labs and complete the labs (since that's all you're graded on)

Forrest is a really nice guy, and a good teacher. His lectures didn't always seem to relate to the labs, but that's ok. The labs were a lot of work, but the help of the TA's and Forrest made them do-able. Super helpful, and gives plenty of opportunity to earn back any points lost if needed. I went from a 60 to a 90 on an exam with the extra credit!

forrest was a great professor! it was easy to contact him outside of class and labs were graded fairly with opportunities to correct them for some points back. he was a funny professor and cared about his students. 100% recommend taking him for gis!!!

analysis.name: Paul Gunnells
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 30 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Gunnells is so goated ngl. The class is hard and he moves at rapid speed, so definitely go to his lectures (echo360 didn't work in this class for me). He explains the concepts really well tho. Exams & gradings are fair. Lots of homework but it earns good amount of credits. Hes not very accessible out of class I think. SI sessions are very helpful.

Super good prof, fantastic lectures and very fair tests. The course moves blisteringly fast and there is quite a lot of homework but he is good about moving hw deadlines back when topics haven't been covered yet.
Feedback on exam mistakes is minimal. You need to read the textbook and do every. single. practice problem in there or be a calculus wiz to get an A.
Chiller prof. Taught the class well and was a somewhat lenient grader. No complaints really.

he is certainly not there to babysit but is more than happy to help. one of the best professors i have had so far. the course material can get tough, especially the homework, but he always accepts questions after class or at his office hours. i would recommend to anyone who is willing to work hard and enjoys math

analysis.name: Govind Srimathveeravalli
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Get ready for a midterm that will ask you questions you could hardly expect even after going through all lecture notes and study material. You will need to look at the formula sheet and then practice all types of questions from the optional textbook to even pass.

For MIE 313
Speaks in riddles. He will answer your question with another question that has nothing to do with what you asked. Also to figure out what is expected of you on projects get ready to perform a scavenger hunt through 50+ forum posts since any comment he makes there will be assumed as common knowledge for the whole class. Unnecessary exam
He doesn't give enough problems for you to practice on, hence why the midterm average is usually very low.

I really enjoyed this class. Just go to lectures and pay attention since he doesnt post class recordings. Start early on the homeworks sometimes they're a lot of work. You get assigned project groups for the entire semester.

Very nice and hilarious, homework was not too hard but could be confusing sometimes. Class overall isn't too difficult but takes up a large amount of time to do well in. The midterm was tough but scaled pretty hard, the final project was graded extremely generously. Not the hardest class, but expect to put in a lot of time to do well.

analysis.name: Mordecai Golin

review_highlights.comment: Professor Golin is by far the best Professor I've had at UMass. He made 210 and 250 much easier to navigate and study despite the very difficult course load. He's also super helpful via office hours and email.

Professor Mordecai is a good DSA professor. His lectures and slides are well organized. The slides are really informative, but the lecture is a little slow-paced. He does not post any past exams, but his study guide contains all the content you need to know for the exams and quizzes. He is also really accessible via email.

The homework is a LOT and the material is not always the easiest, but he does a good job teaching the content. The lectures can feel a bit unfocused on occasion but they're usually well delivered and informative. Ultimately he does a very good job teaching, and the hard part of the class is the workload rather than understanding his lectures.

I love Mordecai. 250 is a difficult course but it's my favorite I've taken at UMass, all thanks to him. His lectures are clear, well-paced, and relevant to the homework/exams. The tests in this class are quite straightforward, just start homework early and ask for help when stuck. Definitely take him instead of Barrington, or just go to his lecture

Professor Golin is a genuine, helpful person. The lectures were very faced paced and can seem intimidating. Overall, very time consuming course but interesting.

analysis.name: Gazi Uddin

review_highlights.comment: Very nice guy, but very boring and tough lectures to sit through. He isn't super knowledgeable about what he's speaking about, and often struggles to answer specific questions that students have.

Gazi was a character. As a teacher, his lectures would be a little boring as he would just read the slides, but as a person, he was a super nice guy. Gazi is one of the nicest people I have met. Although his lectures were sometimes boring, he gave enough work to make us understand why we were learning it. His slides had good amount of information and his tests were based off his slides.
Such a boring class. Gazi is nice but lectures were unbearable because all he did to teach was read off the slides.

analysis.name: Ghazaleh Parvini

Funny professor with clear gift for teaching and explaining complex topics like graph theory, dynamic programming and more in a clear and accessible fashion for students. analysis.name: Stephen Gencarella

review_highlights.comment: Well this was weird. We were only graded on two papers throughout the semester. The only people who did poorly were all the Kyles and Brads who didn't show up.

COMM 248- Folklore of New England.
The class itself is fairly interesting HOWEVER if you miss a single class and dont do the make up work he will drop your grade by one letter. An A becomes and A-. A- becomes a B. Assessed on three responses and a project of our choosing for a grade we decided in March.

This class was very interesting and I loved the professor. One of the BEST professors at umass. I took both his folklore of alcohol and New England classes. Defiantly take any of his classes if you can!!!

says attendance is mandatory but never takes it. No exams just 5 papers, last is the final. Got A's on my papers so far but I put a good amount of effort in. analysis.name: Gabriela Vieyra

Would not recommend taking any classes from this professor. Shows heavy favoritism towards certain students. Makes rude & demeaning comments to students. She grades very unfairly, and insults her students. This professor should be reviewed by the school.

Wow. Had to download this app just to say what an awful profesor Gabriella is. Never in my life have I dealt with such a stressful, infuriating class. The most unfair and unapproachable professors I have ever had. don't bother taking the course, she belittles students and is not very understanding, she expects you have to have a foundation, the grading is very subjective, she will say it is fine then take points off, does not explain what anything means, the homework gets points off on the little things like format, do not take, it is a stressful class

analysis.name: Grigory Hakimov

review_highlights.comment: Making a Global World was a wonderful course! I appreciated that the course materials included a variety of sources, such as readings, podcasts, and videos. Nice guy but do yourself a favor and take anyone else for junior year writing. The most writing I've had in any class, while other professors had barely any assignments. He's not a terribly hard grader but rubrics aren't the most clear. Had a pretty solid A in the class until the last 2 assignments.

Not the best lecturer but a good teacher. Learned cool stuff. Assignments are extremely straightforward and always clearly outlined making it kind of impossible to not do well unless you don't read or follow directions!
The course helped me improve my writing skills. The prompts for assignments are clear. If you follow the instructions, you get good grades. His lectures clearly explain the assigned readings.

I have learned a lot in this class. The topics on the history of international relations were interesting and relevant to current issues. I enjoyed analyzing primary sources and writing papers for this course.

analysis.name: Laura Francis

review_highlights.comment: Laura is the worst professor I have ever had. She wants students to obtain a greater understanding of biology, yet she doesn't give any tools to do so. I would never take one of her classes again. Exams are all open response and often have random details pulled that she hasn't gone over. Content isn't hard but exams are. Wastes SO much class time.

Her exams are insanely difficult, all open response. 2nd exam average  65%. Quizzes are very tricky out of 20 Q. But you will learn to work harder. Increase your determination. Make sure you are "metacognitively" ready for this class. If you are planning to take this class, I recommend the instant noodle and caffeine dependent starter kit.

I overthought every single question I got wrong on every exam. The questions are worded so poorly and thus do not accurately assess the student's knowledge. 100% open response is ridiculous. Partial credit doesn't help either as the exams are graded ridiculously hard. Good luck... It's a 200 level class Laura chill out

Avoid this class!!! She's super unfair with the students and doesn't curve the overall grade when the class exam average is 60 or below. The class material is fine but boom the exam is super hard and nothing like we are taught in discussions or class.

Professor Francis's class is not meant to be an introductory bio class. analysis.name: John Hosp

Prof Hosp tackled remote learning in real time, making adjustments as needed and letting all students know he was there for us! He was such a sweet man and made some great jokes, keeping what was a mundane course somewhat fun.

analysis.name: Heath Hatch

review_highlights.comment: great professor. gives students every opportunity to get an A. Easy to get an A in this class but near IMPOSSIBLE to understand what you're actually doing in this class.

Grade consists of 3 things; Class attendance, homework, and exam grades. The first exam is very difficult, but the last 2 (and the final) are very easy. The lowest exam grade also gets dropped. Attend class and do the homework though; I ended up with an A- only because I skipped two days of class when we had an inclass lab.

Really chill professor. Doesn't lecture much so most of what you learn is from the hw and group assignments. Exams are all based on hw and assignment problems. Lots of extra credit. Lowest test gets dropped so most people didn't even need to take the final. Put in some effort and it's an easy A.

I did no work in this class and got an A. That being said, I hate that the class is TBL. I pay sooo much money just to sit in a room with a highly qualified professor who does nothing and I have to talk to other students who don't know what's going on. Wish at least some days were lecture...

analysis.name: Meghan Huber
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

Meghan Huber is a very fair professor. HW isn't based on correctness, an attempt and a self graded response with solutions she posts. analysis.name: Martin Hunter

Dr. Hunter's Intro to BME class was a great intro to engineering. His lectures were informative & his grading was fair. Labs were easy but I would recommend attending every lab & lecture, both are needed to do well.

Dr. Hunter knows what he is talking about, and does a really job explaining things and breaking things down. The class was a decent amount of work, mostly at the end of the semester, but it was really manageable. Not a lot of homework or reading.

analysis.name: Christiane Meyer Healey

Professor Tillman is honestly one of my favorites, his class is easy to digest and understand. He feels like he truly cares for his students and does his best to create a vibrant and engaging environment. The course work was fairly easy and I was never stressed about an assignment, 10/10.

one of my favorite prefessors teaching some of the best classes at umass; a hard grader but an excellent educator;

analysis.name: Chris Ayala

One of the most influential professors I've had at UMass. Keeps class interesting and fun, teaches so many lessons about life, and is overall just a good human. I would recommend taking this class strictly because of him.

112 was pretty much the only class this semester that I actually looked forward to attending. Absolutely amazing woman. A bit daunting at first, especially as a freshman, but she allows you to catch on quick, and forces you to study via means of daily homework/quizzes. Tough class. Of course, if you're coming out of 126, you already know this, and have resigned yourself to a semester of nonstop studying. analysis.name: Eugene Bagdasarian

Great course if you're interested in the intersection of AI and security. Guest lectures were cool. Well designed course although this was his first iteration of it.

Prof. Baykur is a great professor and a very nice guy. The class has a lot of concepts so don't fall behind but attending his lectures and reading the online textbook is all you need to do well in this class.

Dr. Beltaire is hands down on the of the best professors I've ever had. Her lectures were engaging and very interesting. She's very passionate and knowledgeable and easy to talk to. Danielle Blackman is an awesome teacher. She is very understanding and knows how to teach English well. English is not my first language and I still got a 4.0 in her class. Attend class daily, put time into your papers , and you will get your 4.0!
Words can't describe this class.  We have an awesome time together, and I wish we could keep taking this class into the future.  Awesome, Awesome time.

analysis.name: John Blickford
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: John is kind and funny, and he doesn't make things overly difficult or complicated. 4 exams, and you get two chances to do a makeup exam if you aren't happy with your grade. He does surprise reaction papers during class but there are 9 total and I think only 4 or 5 are necessary, so if you miss class one day you should be okay.

Bickford was great! Sometimes his class was a little dull but I could always follow what he was saying. If you have a chance to take one of his classes, take it. His tests are open note and the grades aren't just based on tests which is always good for getting a better grade.

Bickford is engaging, funny, and makes class enjoyable. You do something interactive every class, including PRS and Reaction Worksheets you need to pass in, which count towards your grade. It's a fun psych class, & he allows cheat sheets on all exams.
His last name is Bickford so i think there was a typo but he is overall a great professor. I have taken two of his classes and his grading criteria is clear and feedback is always given.
best professor ever. he's super engaging with the class and funny. the tests are open note and exactly like the notes and textbook readings.

analysis.name: Christopher Boone
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 55 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Class is easy and lectures are good but he talks really fast and doesn't allow laptops. Discussions are the most helpful and what will help you really learn. A good bit of homework but it's not hard a lot is for completion and easy grading. Tests aren't bad but definitely need to study don't go in blind. Do the homework and you will be fine.

Super nice guy, talks soooo fast. That man is not on speed, he is speed. But the lectures are posted. Lots of hw but it's not hard, good to raise your grade. Put in the effort and you'll do fine. Prof Boone rlly loves what he teaches lol.

This class was my hardest class so far but that's simply because I have absolutely no background in economics, and took stats instead of calc in high school. Lectures are packed with info and go pretty fast. DO NOT SKIP a lecture if you value your sanity. Discussion classes mandatory, exams scaled, extra credit, lecture heavy, and good teacher.

Boone gives a lot of outside work to do but it's all related to what will be on exams and to help you understand the material or help get you ready for lecture. The weekly problem sets are annoying, but if you do all of them and do all the other homework you will do fine. He curves exams by a lot too.

Boone is a great lecturer, but it can be hard to get a chance to talk to him due to the sheer class size. 
You generally don't need to attend lectures, but he usually explains content better than the study guide's do. 
Your grade is in large part based around your score on exams and a small number of problem sets.

analysis.name: Semih Boz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: He's a great guy that cares about his students. Very flexible and if you reach out to him he is always ready to help. Attendance is not mandatory but he gives pop quizzes like once a week. However, he moves very quickly and is not the best at teaching. Does not slow down for students, kind of goes at his own pace.

Semih is a great guy. Took the class in the spring of 2024; not sure what has changed but he was always easy to reach outside of class and genuinely cared about the students who made a connection with him. He does have pop quizzes and the tests are annoying but overall if you prep for them and ask questions you should be fine.

Great person who is very understanding and cares about his students. Understands that the material is difficult and tries to make it as understandable as possible. Very flexible on homework assignments and tests understands you may need extra help.

analysis.name: Boone Shear
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 51 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Class was really easy,  minimal hw just a weekly reading and a writing response, one small paper, and "exams" were t/f take homes. No recorded lectures or slides are posted, so I don't recommend skipping too often. That said, lectures were super repetitive and I'm not sure I really learned anything. TAs do the majority of the grading.

The class isn't hard, and assignments are easy, but lectures feel pointless. He won't upload slides or allow technology, stopping class if anyone uses a device. It feels childish, like we're in high school. He also goes on random political rants, which makes the class uncomfortable(I say this as a very liberal guy btw)

This was my favorite class taken so far at Umass! This professor was amazing. He is so kind and makes the class actually enjoyable. Attendance isn't mandatory however, attend lecture because the tests are all about what he talks about. The Ta's graded papers and gave no feedback. Papers due every Monday but they are easy. Love this class!!!!

Boone is a great guy, however his class is tough. On average, he gives about 3 five page essaysarticles to read every week. Also this is a writing intensive course so expect to write papers every week. If you are a slow reader, or a bad writer, please listen to me and do not take this class, save your GPA.

I honestly didn't enjoy this class very much. Its possible that Anthro just isn't for me, but I found most of the material to be very pedantic and boring, and generally the class felt kind of pointless. Boone is kind and the coursework wasn't too difficult despite this. Weekly journal/response activities, manageable readings, easy final and midterm

analysis.name: Susan Boyer
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Boyer's class is great! You work through the in-class assignments together and she makes sure you understand how to get to the final answer (she's always happy to go through the problem again if you need more clarification). Incredibly nice professor and you can tell she loves to teach the material.

One of the best professors I have had at the school. There are a lot of assignments, this class will take up a good amount of time. But these assignments do a fantastic job having you learn the content. I learned a ton in this class and was never too worried about my grade. Also very accessible outside of class for any help.

So much of what makes an excellent instructor is mastery of the subject. Susan is without question, both incredibly deft at data management, however, also a prolific teacher. She was an excellent facilitator of problem-solving, very responsive, and downright interested in her students' success- however, such is earned in this class - not a gimmie.
All the work was very relevant and easy to complete correctly if you follow the directions. Easy A and you will learn some cool excel tricks too.

analysis.name: Kerri Bohonowicz
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 55 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: kerri is an amazing teacher! super understanding, easy grader, and makes the course easily digestible. i was dreading this course before enrolling given my absolute hatred for numbers and zero background in accounting, but she made it very interesting esp by weaving in her own experience in the industry. go to lectures for tophat questions!

Lectures weren't the most exciting, but I did learn a lot. The quizzes weren't bad, but you definitely need to study! She is a caring professor and wants students to succeed!

Kerri is very sweet and does a good job in helping us learn material. In my opinion she made the material a bit hard to udnerstand in her lecture, the homework videos are definately way more helpful. She provides a ton of study resources for her quizzes. My TA kind of sucked since she went through the labs so quickly (Shira). Def take Kerri tho.

I absolutely love her and she is a gem, its easy to do well in this class and she is my most organized professor.

She makes me excited to go to class and she is so sweet.

She talks very clearly and confidently and knows her material. 

I wanna be like her when I grow up. 

She also communicates well and has many awesome T'A's.

#ChangedMajor

Professor Bohonowicz was a great teacher; I learned a lot. There are usually 2 homework assignments per week. There is usually a quiz every couple of weeks (5 total in the semester), which consists of 10 multiple-choice questions. Overall, this class was difficult, but if you pay attention in lecture and study, you should be fine.

analysis.name: Dee Boyle-Clapp
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

review_highlights.comment: She genuinely cares about her students and consistently asked us for feedback. She can be a little disorganized, but she always helps clear up confusion if you ask her.

For anyone who is interested in arts management, this class is a great introduction! Dee is an amazing person and very knowledgeable in the field. The directions she gave in class were not always clear.
Good introduction to arts management. Expensive textbook required. Fair amount of homework and graded on attendance. Often unclear what is due and when. She is very friendly and helpful!

analysis.name: Phuthipong Bovornkeeratiroj
analysis.verdict: Tough course, but students consistently rate the teaching highly, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: I didn't enjoy this class very much but that was almost solely because of the course setup itself and Joe's structuring. Nikko is a very caring person, and a decent lecturer. He is helpful outside class and is clearly trying to improve. 100% take this course with him and NOT with Joe. Nikko's slides are better.

By far the most authentically caring and nice professor I've met. He made his lectures very fun and when I did go to class it was just for the good vibes. Not everyone (myself included) is a big fan of systems, but the labs and homework aren't toooo bad if your C is strong. The exams were very fair and I was able to self study pretty successfully.

Nikko's lectures were fun and engaging, there were many opportunities for extra credit, and the "4 picks 2" policy made getting an A very comfortable and achievable. The textbook is wonderful and freely published online, the projects were all relevant and instructive, and the final was very fair. A great experience and I learned a lot.

The most genuine and caring professor ever. Nikko makes this course more interesting and fun by adding some animations and memes to the lecture slides. Really approachable and always care about our well-being. He makes the process of learning low-level programming a bit more enjoyable. If you're looking to take 230, definitely take with Nikko
Nikko is great, highly recommend taking 377 with him. He takes his time lecturing and makes sure you understand the material, and is a super nice guy.

analysis.name: Brenna Casey
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 15 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: extremely supportive in helping students construct better writing. im convinced that the reviews stating she is mean are misconstruing her dry sense of humor. she was nothing but respectful toward my class. she does have expectations for class conduct and how assignments should be submitted, but they are reasonable and easy to follow

Arguably one of the worst professors I have ever had. She didn't grade anything throughout the semester, was terrible at clarifying discussion topics in class, and overall had a terrible attitude. She was not funny, not charming, and would belittle students who may not have had the analytical skills she expected. 0/10, will NEVER see her again!

I can see how some students might not like her personality, but I enjoyed her class. Really intelligent professor. Big final project, not bad if you don't leave until the last minute.

Brenna is the best professor I've ever had hands down. She's an absolute legend. I've never felt so inspired to write before, and everything we read for class was amazing. Discussions were so funny but also very thoughtful. If you take her class you're in for a treat, also you should look up some pictures of walt whitman because that will come up:)

Brenna is my favorite teacher at UMass.She is very smart but lectures in a way that helps students understand by simplifying complex history.Every assignment is predictable,she is clear about grading,she gets assignments back to us with extensive notes within two weeks of submitting it, she is flexible with extensions, always open to office hours!

analysis.name: Bridgette Davis
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took Prof. Davis for SPP341- she's great. She genuinely cares about her students and wants you to learn. The course load is very manageable, and it's heavily discussion based so you feel like you're apart of the lessons. Definitely a class where you'll learn a lot.

Bridgette was an excellent professor and I really enjoyed her class. Long readings, but if you didn't do them it was ok. The class was conversation heavy, really helpful in understanding my experience as a young adult. As an intro to the SPP major, I expected it to be more focused on policymaking, but I still had a great experience!

Professor Davis inspires a lot of interest in the material of her courses, she's very well versed within the world of social sciences, politics, etc. She runs her classes in an engaging way that makes the course work fun, I highly recommend her classes!

Professor Davis is incredible. Classes discuss the readings due for that day. All topics are relevant and meaningful to young adults/the world. 3 short papers are due throughout the semester, with time given in class to work on them and ask questions. Provides space for students to engage in large and small group discussions.  Take this class!

She is an amazing professor who truly cares about her students and the course work. They were focused on student growth and comprehension about big social issues. Readings for every class, but they aren't difficult and are discussed at length in class. Assignments are not hard and she is very open to questions and feedback.

analysis.name: Bruno da Silva
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining

He's incredible. Students don't deserve him. I fell in love with RL because he makes everything so accessible and insightful. Just showing up to class made me feel like I understood everything. His quick reviews at the start of each lecture helped so much. I hope he knows how inspiring he is. for anyone at UMass, Take this class!

Makes complex topics actually approachable and exciting. You can tell he genuinely cares - he stays after class for hours answering questions and making sure everyone understands the material. Highly recommend taking any class he teaches!

Chill dude though, is sympathetic and has a reasonable syllabus
Hands down one of the best professors at UMass. 687 is a must take course!

analysis.name: Brenda Garcia
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit

Intersting class and very easy-going professor. Had some obligations through the semester, but reaching out for help she was able to help accommodate and was understanding.
