She is very passionate about what she teaches. They are super accommodating to anything allow late work. You have one assignment a week and a paper as a final.Some readings are long but we would take a whole week to discuss so you could space out the reading .They were a bit unorganized but could be due to this being their first sem teaching here.

Legal 275, although at times disorganized and confusing, was interesting and looked at a ton of real world examples throughout lectures and reading. You will have a short 250 word reflection every week but most of the time it can be done in class time.  The professor herself as very kind and clearly cared about the success of the students.

analysis.name: John Bickford
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 487 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: I don't understand how some people are honestly complaining that the class was too easy? Do you know how dumb ya'll sound? The man is funny, the content is interesting, and you have to be the biggest bum on the planet to not pass this class! It's like you idiots want to drown in homework and stress over exams

Professor Bickford really cares about making his classes enjoyable for his students. He understands the stress students are under, and he really just cares about teaching on topics he loves. Highly recommend taking any course you can with him. Cheat sheets for tests, allows room to miss a few homeworks & iclicker sessions, no final.
AMAZING. FANTASTIC. WONDERFUL. I LOVE HIM. AMAZING CLASS. 10/10, WOULD TAKE AGAIN.
4 Exams allowed with a cheat sheet each. Homework is pretty easy and the lectures are interesting. Go to class for i clickers and response questions, they aren't hard.

Prof. Bickford is a solid choice for a psych professor. He is very lenient with extra credit and doesn't usually assign a lot of homework. His tests are open note but even then they're not very hard. He really cares about his students and is very engaging throughout class. You don't need the text book much; just show up, do the HW and you'll pass.

analysis.name: Erin Butler
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Great choice for a CICS305 instructor. Professor Butler was a wonderful professor who was very compassionate towards her students and showed high flexibility towards student situations by making herself easy to contact outside office hours and encouraging a judgment-free learning environment in class. Very charismatic, I enjoyed this class a lot.

This woman is a savior for any computer science student who wants to avoid Michelle Trim for 305. If you can take 305 with Professor Butler, please do! Organized course structure, reasonable workload, flexible accessibility outside class and office hours, and welcoming learning environment. I'll take classes with Butler again if I have a chance.

Such a sweet lady!! You can tell Professor Butler genuinely wants her students to be successful and is very easy to contact outside class. She always helps me a lot, and I revise my papers based on her feedback. It works! As long as you put full effort into the papers and participate consistently, she will know. And your grade can be paid off.

She is by far the most humble and down-to-earth professor I have seen in the English department. Prof Butler was always open for deep ethical discussions and never placed a students' view beneath her own's. 
Her feedback for graded assignments is extremely useful. I found it easy to review my work to receive better grades based off her feedback.

It is clear she cares about her students, grading is more than fair, and there is an extremely generous extension policy. Lectures frequently involve discussion and generative writing so you are not sitting and listening for very long at a time, which is good. Definitely take 305 with her.

analysis.name: Brian Sargent
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 36 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: If I see Sargent in hell, I won't even say hi. His class grade is only based on 3 exams with 25-30 questions that are poorly worded and more than one right answer. He does not reply to emails, or care about his students at all. I took this class as a pre med and its harder to score than my toughest science classes.

Not the best gen ed to take if you're looking for an easy A. Grade is based on 3 exams and no extra credit. Exams are only around 30 questions long and some of the questions aren't even based on his lectures! You can't even watch the lectures until you email him and have an excuse. Not a flexible class and doesn't explain lecture materials well.

goes way too fast in lectures, makes lecture notes extensively long (my hand is cramping as we speak), refuses to posts lecture videos online unless you emailed him you were absent ahead of time (can't rewatch lectures to study for exam), gives no study guide or any help when preparing for exam. 2/10 do not recommend.

Professor Sargent is an excellent, organized teacher. His lectures are super engaging. His course builds practical historical research skills through a semester-long project. Brian is a fair grader who gives personalized feedback, even in a large class, and shows genuine care for students. Highly recommended.

I enjoyed Brian's Social Inequality Policy course. He's an amazing lecturer who intentionally chose his words and engaged well with students' questions. The readings and lectures were dense, but all of them were very helpful for my understanding of the subject. I find myself referencing back to this class very often. I recommend him to any friends.

analysis.name: Brenda Bushouse

analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 41 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Worst teacher I have ever had. She makes horrible comments to students on assignments and is overall a terrible professor. I would strongly advise anyone taking a class with her.

prof bushouse is one of the worst profs Ive ever had. guidelines to assignments are never clear, & her lectures are completely disorganized & all over the place. she acts like a high school teacher, looking over students shoulders to see what they're doing on their computer & monitors students in a stalking way in class. highly do not recommend.
.

I took a 1 credit class with her. WORST TEACHER. I mean, she's really into her work, but if she doesn't like you, you'll know it...and that will affect your grade. Book was $100+ and hardly used. AVOID BRENDA. Heels on linoleum made us flinch by the end of her class.

Took the first ever SPP capstone course with Professor Bushouse and enjoyed it. While there were kinks to be worked out (first ever SPP capstone), she was very accomodating and caring as long as you communicated with her. I would definitely take her again. Show up, get the books, use class time wisely and you will get a lot out of the course.

Course itself is a good one. Instructor isn't best suited to teach it although very knowledgeable. What should be easy class content becomes tedious/ambiguous. Students are an afterthought re structure of course content/pace of assignments. No real review for exams/rare use of rubrics. TAs integral to student success. Take PS383 for policy instead.

analysis.name: Gulten Busra Karkili
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently

review_highlights.comment: She wants everyone to do well. Sometimes spent too long lecturing, leaving us with only 15-20 minutes to do the quiz of classwork. Overall nice and not a bad experience.

A very sweet and patient teacher who takes the time to ensure that her students understand the content. Gives opportunties for extra credit and very flexible with students individual needs. Also she has a great sense of humor.
She was an amazing professor this semester. She does in class excel exercises and makes sure everyone knows what they're doing and gives help if needed. Highly recommended
Super friendly and wants all of her students to do well. Exams and quizzes are open-note, and they are not that hard.
Laid-Back Class, she cares a lot about students and wants them to learn! Put in the work, and you will do well

analysis.name: Wayne Burleson

I went to him to understand some concepts and he couldn't explain them to me and didn't even bother to look into it afterwards.  He has top level knowledge of the course but not in depth.

Cool guy but lectures aren't very helpful. He expects you to already know some of the stuff he's talking about. Very easy grading tho. One final and the rest of your grade is made up of easy hws and quizzes. He lets you to drop some of your lower grades. Attendance is graded but you also have 3 free absences. Shouldn't be hard to get a good grade.

The first 2/3 of 547 involves reading research papers that Burleson will then just point to keywords from during lecture, not contributing much else. Then the amount of time you get for the final project is way too short, and the project is super rushed. This class is pretty easy, but if you really want to learn about security take CS 390R.
Took it because of degree requirement, but really like it

analysis.name: Michele Burch

She knows her stuff and will work with you to help you succeed. Definitely the best professor I've had in any OIM class so far. Would recommend.

Michele Burch thinks she is charming... she is not. Even though this class is mandatory, it is the worlds most useless content if you are not an OIM major. BBL is very clear, highly organized, and clearly cares about students. Moderate challenge but manageable

This impacts tuition assistance for folks that are company sponsored.

You get assigned weekly reading with questions and that what you do in discussion. Theres 3 tests and thats it. You need to actually talk in discussion or your grade is bad. Seems bad, but good GenEd

This "guilty until proven innocent" attitude goes against everything an institution of higher education should stand for and calls into question Bunk's priorities (and ability to see).

analysis.name: Andreas Buttenschoen

I'm just trying to post a comment

analysis.name: Moises Bustos

analysis.name: CJ Llego

analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This was my favorite class last semester. CJ got us thinking about how to be happy in and out of his class; his class was engaging, fun and made me think about why we make the choices we make in our writings and lives. He's an open book and always made us laugh with his stories and helped me get a summer internship. Best professor at this school.

Great overall, he makes a hated first year class amazing and fun every lecture. There are only a few major essays which you really need to worry about and he exteneds if need be. Also his conferences tell you exactly what you need to do to get an A on the paper. The best thing about CJ is that he is more a peer than a prof.

I loved taking his class. There are a lot of essays but he broke is down in to smaller assignments and was helpful in conferences. He told funny stories to make the class more comfortable and connected them to my essays. Thank you for everything!
CJ helped me realize my true writing ability by allowing me the right amount of freedom and guidance. I owe him my continuing passion for the written word.

analysis.name: William Clement
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 22 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Probably one of the worst courses I have taken at Umass. The labs are very tedious and often have you doing mindless calculations for the sake of nothing. It's not particularly difficult but it is the worst class I have taken at Umass. It's no wonder the geology department recruits so hard with this intro class, it's easy to see its not any good.

I did not enjoy this class at all! Only took Dynamic Earth for a Gen. Ed. but it was super boring. He only has 4 Exams drops the lowest grade which is 90% of your grade, and a few assignments that require you to write two sentences worth 10% of your grade. The "textbook" was a Geology novel that I did not read but 1 or 2 Q's are on the exams fromit

This class is one of the worst classes I have taken so far. Labs are long and tedious and boring. The teacher in the lectures just talks a lot and the lectures are REALLY boring and that's the reason the lecture hall is always more than half empty. There are no study guides or anything before the exams either and a lot of homework.

I would really avoid taking any class with this professor at all cost. The lectures slide make absolutely no sense outside of the context of the lecture, this would be fine if he did not fly through the material and you could take notes at a reasonable pace (I write fast). The echo 360's have no sound which makes them useless. The test are ok.

Has a lot of boring assignments that are due each week but are easy and can be completed in less than 15 minutes a week. The lectures are boring so make sure to study the slides if you don't go to class. There are 4 tests but 1 drops and there is group portion. Lab is easy when you go to office hours so they can help you.

analysis.name: Justin Clarke
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Professor Clarke is passionate about what he teaches and fully explains everything. The material was difficult for me to grasp as it was an introductory course about AI; however, it was just a first-year seminar, so the course's assignments simply consisted of easy weekly readings. He was happy to answer questions and gave feedback to each student.

Justin Clarke was the TA for CS348 and is the best one I have had thus far. He is genuinely helpful on Piazza and easy to talk to. When the professor was busy, Justin was usually fast to respond on Piazza and took time to clarify any misconceptions people have during his office hours.

A great TA who's quite helpful in office hours, although it does take time for him to post stuff on Moodle. 348 is pretty laid-back and if you simply do the work and go to his office hours, you will do well.

analysis.name: Tyler Clark
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: FYS How Gay Culture is Made. Very passionate, kind, caring, funny, etc. Just a great guy. No big assignments or HW in this class. Great environment. Just a PSA this course is more abt gay pop culture history (think drag and camp) rather than gay history vibes. Would def take his class again.
Had him for the Gay Culture first year seminar. He was passionate about everything he taught. Radiates the most positive energy.

I took him for his English 131, outgoing and loud professor who is passionate about what he teaches. Class was fairly easy, but also he keeps it involved and its not dead in the classroom. 3 books, 3 essays. You can also skip class he takes attendance randomly.
RECOMMEND TAKING THIS CLASS. Tyler is a really nice professor, the materials are really interesting to learn

Very very very nice profesor. Take his first year seminar, way easier than everyone else's that I know. Very chill dude, you legit just have to show up. I think there was 2 assignments which were each 30 second presentations where you could stay in your seat.

analysis.name: Chris McDaniel
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 360 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: This Lab class was such a joke of a class, but your grade is mostly determined by your TA. The Owls are easy, the experiments are stupidly long and tedious. The final was only 20 questions and a handful were on the stupidest topics that were barely discussed. It's clearly a requirement class or you wouldn't be taking it. Stupidly time consuming.

Very rude person. Doesn't help you if you are in trouble. He will make you feel you are damn stupid, and he doesn't care what you feel. Don't reply the e-mail which he thinks this problem he doesn't care. You'd better to deal with your TA more than him. If take this course, try not deal with him in person. I will piss you off.

Honestly the guy is very clearly a research professor and I frankly don't blame hime for making this class a pain. However good lord this is simple chemistry but you would think it's some kind of a divinchi code. He completely lacks any understanding whatsoever and just has absolutely no real social skills.
Chris McDaniel is probably the biggest sore loser when it comes to professors in the orgo field of the chemistry department.

Chem lab was the biggest waste of my time. The experiments themselves were fine, however the lab reports along with prelab work, OWLs, post lab OWLs, and LUH hours is too much for a 2 credit course, oh and the unnecessary final. Extremely strict attendance rules, you cannot be late or submit any late work past 3 days. My TA made the lab bearable.

analysis.name: Jeffrey Clark
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 42 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Professor Clark is dedicated to helping students learn and trying to give them skills that will actually benefit them in their future careers. Class was lectures on Mondays and group presentations on Wednesday. Large portion of the grade was made up of large case studies.

Great guy with lots of knowledge/connections in the industry. He is a great resource to go to for guidance. In Business In Society, the class typically consists of one group presentation per week, and he leaves his projects up to interpretation.

Class has 3 exams and that is your grade. Exams are no walk in the park so if your a bad test taker I wouldn't reccomend unless you are going into real estate. He is very knowledgeable about real estate but this class is not easy by any means, so only take it if you have an interest in real estate.
Great teacher, made going to an 8:30 class somewhat easy. Class is pretty test heavy but the material is not insanely difficult if you pay attention in class.

Professor Clark is very understanding and respectful, so never be afraid to ask him for guidance or support! He took the time to get to know everyone in class. He is an easy grader who mainly assigns group projects and some self reflections in between classes. Very easy class and easygoing professor.

analysis.name: Carey Clouse
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class was awesome! It had weekly readings which were short, 1 20 min presentation, and a 2 page paper. She's been all over the world, so she has really cool input on a lot of things. She also brought tea to every class! I would definitely recommend this class

Awesome professor, and I had a fantastic experience. Best 391A at Umass.  Discussion based seminar, great readings and only a interesting presentation is what you are responsible for. HIGHLY recommend.

Carey is one of the best options for a professor choice for the honors 1-credit discovery seminar. Fair, respectful, understanding, and cares about her students. She asks for participation but won't force it if you don't want to talk. Put in some effort and engage with the readings, and this 391AH section will probably hand you an A no problem.
Worst professor I've ever had. Grading made no sense, didn't have a lesson plan, etc. Disorganized and I learned nothing. Didn't respond to emails or verbal attempts to discuss issues or questions.
Carey was such an amazing prof. She was super caring and considerate of what we could do after a year of virtual learning. I learned so much from her and my classmates from this class!

analysis.name: Claudia Wilson
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: This professor cared about my growth as a writer. I enjoyed the readings because it was a diverse group of writers. I also felt like some students didn't take this course seriously because a lot of them skipped. It wasn't like my life was changed, but I could see a marked difference before and after the course. I would take this class again.

This Professor really cared about my writing. I read a lot, but can tell a marked difference in my writing before entering this course and after. It didn't change my life, but I could see the difference. Some students complained about the reading, but they were great because they also gave extra credit for falling behind.

I esp liked folks reviewing my paper and the different things I would see. I think this professor could work on some things, but overall was decent, and I would take them again. I also took their poetry class and I appreciate the variety of diverse readers we read together in class!

I enjoyed this class because the assignments seemed fair and even though I wasn't a writing major. I learned a lot from the readings. I would take this course if it was more reading based than writing. This professor made me laugh and helped me ease into writing papers.

Avoid if you can. Easy A, but nothing of value is gained from taking English 356 with them. Cancelled at least 6 classes over the semester (almost always cancelled classes just before they were supposed to start) and late to the rest of classes (usually 10 minutes). No constructive feedback from professor during workshops either. Waste of time.

analysis.name: Clare Hammonds
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 3 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: She was a very good teacher in class, very fun and lively. HOWEVER, She never responds to emails, none whatsoever. She also never grades anything, all assignments were graded the day grades were due. There is a lot of work without any directions, its a guessing game. Overall, she seems like a nice person just all over the place.

She's a really good professor, and the class is not difficult at all, it's one of those classes where you feel like the professor actually wants you to learn. No "final exam", just a final project that had multiple options. Very sweet lady, and I would recommend the course. She is very passionate about what she teaches.
This class is very heavy on class discussions and 'turning and talking.' Has been a very informative class.

analysis.name: Maria Correia
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 78 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I had Prof. Correia for Math 545 - Advanced linear algebra, and also some lectures of Calc 2(Math 132). She is one of my most awesome lecturers at UMass, though she has a very thick accent, you get used to it in 2-3 lectures, and it never hampers your understanding. She is very excited to teach, and you can literally see that in her lectures.

Her lectures are incredibly helpful. Missing a class is missing a concept because the lectures aren't recorded, but as long as you pay attention and follow along, it is incredibly helpful. It is clear that she cares about her students and will go out of her way to make sure that those who ask for help get the resources they need.

Professor Correia provides solid engaging lectures. The lectures are not recorded, however, notes are provided for each lecture which are very useful as they cover everything you need to know for the exams. She does have a slight accent, however she writes everything on the board. I enjoyed this course and would highly recommend!

Maria was an amazing professor (she's the course chair!). Her lecture slides are incredibly helpful, and the lectures are paced quite well. As long as you attend them and pay attention, you should do well. She was also more than happy to answer students' questions. The course also had a discussion section, which I didn't find too helpful.

Not understanding to student's circumstances. Rigid in policies with no extensions. Took in a summer session. One midterm and one final. 5 quizzes (MC through Webassig/Cengage and Open Response through Gradescope). Used honorlock extension for midterm and final. Final has multiple choice and open response questions. First time got this horrid grade

analysis.name: Claire Norton
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 144 reviews, this is a reliable picture

review_highlights.comment: This class is one of the easiest 3 credits you can get. Prof Norton is hilarious and she explains well what shes teaching and makes directions clear for exams tests etc. Tests are online and the only work assigned are work from the discussion portion (which you have time to do in class), weekly in class writings, and end of the week lecture quizzes

She was such a funny and chill professor def take this class. The only thing was the discussions and TA classes had a lot of work but it wasn't bad, those are mandatory but not lectures. Take this class lowkey easy just lots of online hw and you cant miss any or else your grade will tank. Professor is super nice class was never boring, useful too.

This was a very good and interesting class to take. Professor Norton teaches each concept very well. There are weekly quizzes that you can do on your own time. There are exams but they are take-home. There are also opportunities for extra credit if you need it. She is so understanding and a good/ personable professor.

Claire highlights exactly what will be on the exams in her lecture slides. She gives easy 5 question Moodle quizzes each week, 3 homework assignments, an essay and 3 non-cumulative exams. Most of the discussion section grade is based on attendance, with two group projects.

Great professor! Easy class. Attendance not mandatory but there are random in-class writings, not difficult but annoying if you're looking to skip class. Online quizzes and exams, open notes. I recommend attending class as her slides tell you what are on the quizzes and you don't have to deal with missing a in class writing.

analysis.name: Connolly Ryan
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 79 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Aside from the fact that his humor is stuck in high school and he tries too hard to be "relatable," his ideas on life are pretty complex and deep. I think his lectures get MAD boring by the end because the books you read in his class are all pretty much tied to the same idea. Not much room for discussion. Don't get him started on Hampshire College.

Loved this class! Just 3 papers along with weekly book reading. Had one pop quiz with various threats throughout the semester but none came to fruition. Overall an extremely easy class. Prof Connolly is zany and borderline morbid at times but he took a soul-sucking class and made it fun and engaging. 11/10 would recommend.

Chill and easy A, but I won't lie 201H with Professor Ryan is hugely overrated. You'll get plenty of feedback on papers, which helps grades if you put in effort. However, his Moodle page is basically empty and discussions often turn into long, dry monologues with not enough room for students to talk.

Just show up! You don't even have to talk and you could miss a couple of classes too. He let us out early sometimes. You really will learn a lot about BDIC too. If you an incoming freshman choose this as your seminar it's the easiest A ever!

Prof Ryan was one of my favorite professors. He's super passionate about what he teaches and jokes all the time. Every class is an open discussion consisting of 15% student participation and 85% monologue. Participation isn't mandatory but attendance is. We read three short books and were supposed to write three essays, but ended up writing two.

analysis.name: Heather Conboy
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 11 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Professor Conboy is a kind and understanding instructor who cares about her students and the material she teaches. However, she has high expectations for grading. While the workload isn't terrible, it can be very easy to lose a lot of credit on the homework assignments due to unclear instructions.
She is a down-to-earth professor who is helpful in office hours, but the grading policy is overall too harsh. Would not recommend unless you're a graduate student. (coming from an undergrad student)

It's clear that Prof. Conboy cares about good coding practices and preparing students to be effective engineers. The lecturers aren't super engaging but most of the course is based on the group project. She gives rubrics for each assignment so expectations are clear although grading can be a bit harsh
Most down-to-earth professor in the software engineering field of the CS department. If you are stuck drop by her office hours anytime!

Won't recommend the course. The worst part is the grading, not at all clear and will cut marks on any silly trivial thing. Supposed to be not heavy but there are 8 heavy assignments apart from the weekly participation quiz and a big project. No extra credits. Recorder lectures are inaudible and teaching is superficial.

analysis.name: Elsa Cousins
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Best class I have taken at UMass. Learned more here than in most other classes, and as long as you show up and put in effort, it is an easy class. Also Elsa and the TA are always great at helping out when needed.

Elsa's lectures were kinda dry but she was clearly very knowledgeable on the subject. I was struggling with my group members during a group project and she didn't feel very approachable. The class was fine but there was a lot of textbook readings assigned.
Get to walk outside, actually retain knowledge of plants

This class felt overwhelming at the start of the year, but by the end of the year I was very much ahead on work. I would not have been able to tell you the difference between an oak tree and maple tree at the start of the year. Now I know the difference between oak and maple species and their scientific names. Plus soo much more. Great class
My favorite class yet. I learned a ton, and the class was super fun. Cousins was an amazing teacher. Would absolutely take again.

analysis.name: Thomas Corcoran
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I love Tom. He is so funny and sweet. If you have an issue, he is always ready to help. He loves people who participate, but he won't force it. He does love doing pairs and shares tho. I'm gonna miss him.

10/10 class. Attendance and class participation goes towards your grade but it's fairly interesting material. As long as you read the readings you should be fine. We had one final paper worth 30% of your grade but the weekly homework is a simple reflection on two readings of your choice. Midterm=online! He is very understanding of disabilities too!

Once you get into the swing of things in his course, expectations become very clear and they are easy to meet. There are several papers to write throughout the semester (all pretty spaced out) but that's it for homework. No daily assignments, no quizzes, no exams. All you have to do is read. He seems genuinely interested in what he is teaching too.

analysis.name: Helene Cousin
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 48 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: A lot of content and diagrams on the exam would be pulled from recorded lectures she posted, because she would run out of time during class. Must memorize basically everything for the exams because there are so many potential questions you may see. Her handwriting is difficult to read and she often misspells or forgets parts of a diagram

Her exams were mostly material from the practice quizzes. However, when she would label diagrams in class, she would ask you for things on the exam, that were never gone over in class. You have to go above and beyond to teach yourself the full systems outside of class. The labs also felt unorganized, the TA's never seemed to know what was going on

I came in looking to get a solid basis on animal physiology/anat. Professor Cousin gave inaccurate information, and degraded students. Labs were disorganized, and she put individuals down to gain superiority. Above all, I left this class learning how to deal with the real world's difficult individuals.

I would say don't take this class but unfortunately you probably have to. Dr. Cousin is a nice woman but she cannot teach. Her lectures and labs are very unorganized and you will have to watch additional videos outside of class, as well as get the answers to everything yourself b/c she does not provide her TA's and SIs with the material to help us.

A lot of lecture material but that's anatomy for you! She made the class super enjoyable for me, varying up lecture material with drawing content. Exams were questions taken from the hw quizzes, so an A is achievable! Only downside is it was hard to get in contact with her outside of class, she doesn't look at her email often. Extra credit too!

analysis.name: Christopher Cox
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 35 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: I was signed with disability services to take my chem exam the same time as his class and he threw a temper tantrum and refused for me to take my chem exam the same time as his and in fact blamed it on me while it was disability services who picked that time for me. he also took forever to respond to my emails. HAS THE BIGGEST COMPLEX EVER.

Great man, but terrible professor. Lectures don't really give insight into how to understand the concepts and most of the time I don't understand what he's talking about when going through the examples. The discussion sessions are a lifesaver though, but otherwise, I'd choose a different professor for multi.

Good guy, just a terrible lecturer. I took AP Calc and found myself more confused from his lectures than before. He seems to skip around and go on tangents. I missed quizzes many times and he always let me redo them with no penalty. If you have no calc background, i'd recommend a different professor. No regular exams so HW and quizzes really matter

Professor Cox's lectures tend to make the content more confusing. Had I not had a previous understand of the main concepts of calculus, I would be totally lost in the class. Also, often times he'll spend up to 15 minutes talking about the upcoming schedule. I stopped going to lecture, and found it more informative to take notes from the book.

Genuinely do not take 223 with him. He is a nice dude, but his lectures do not help at all. He goes off topic every 5 mins and does not focus on the stuff we're learning right now. 90% of the time, his examples don't make sense, and he doesn't really explain the concepts first. Homework is a lot at times. You're better off taking another professor.

analysis.name: Csaba Andras Moritz
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This guy is terrible. He is my advisor and my teacher. He is awful at both. He is interested in seeing students learn, but if you have not perfected your knowledge he doesn't give you any credit. He doesn't grade fairly at all. He basically grades with an "A or F" approach. The other teacher for the class is fair so I will get an A in the course.

Prof. Moritz is an expert in the field of computer architecture and his classes provide good intuition for the design challenges in the field. As a processor design engineer, I can unambiguously state that the topics discussed in the class are closely relevant to the industry and provide solid foundation to excel in the field. Very useful course.

One of the best teachers at UMass. He provides intuition for each concept that makes it very easy to understand fundamentally why and how it works, which not many teachers do. Very easy to talk to, patient and approachable. His lectures are always interesting and include lessons from his research and professional experiences.

He is an amazing teacher, and a great mentor. My PhD journey in his group started with his 668 course. The lecture contents include components from traditional computer architecture literature and advanced research topics. I learnt a lot, and I could publish a conference paper out of the course project.
uninterested in teaching, preparing question papers, grading projects and answer sheets..

analysis.name: Craig Nicolson
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Still questioning if this class was one big joke. This was one of the most frustrating experiences ever. The assignments, or serious lack there of, didn't follow the syllabus at all. He doesn't respond to emails. Nothing is on Canvas. Don't know how he's still allowed to teach. Please DON'T take this class or any with Craig, for your own sanity.

Didn't upload half the assignments on the syllabus and never responded to my email. I got a B+ and have no idea why bc only 3 grades got uploaded so now I have to send him another email so I can know why I got the grade I did. Incredibly unorganized, the class meets only once a week and has TAs so idk what he was doing instead of grading.

Never prepared for class + always sweaty- by far the worst class I've taken at UMass. Didnt follow the syllabus or put a single grade in Moodle. I didnt know it was graded attendance till halfway through the semester, p sure he was scrambling to make up grades since he barely assigned anything for us to do. Waste of my time,but at least I got an A

Craig is a really nice guy, but the class was completely disorganized. His lectures were dull and i learned very little. Pretty easy A if you show up for most lectures and participate. Had a few VERY drawn out group assignments. He did not make any criteria for grading clear the whole semester. easy 4 credits (2hr lectures on W/F) but no lab

I don't even know what this class was about. We did a few group projects which were never graded and then one really long group project which was also never graded. Had us read a book to write a review and then never assigned it. Doesn't respond to emails. Nice guy but was completely disorganized. Easy A if you show up to class.

analysis.name: Britt Crow-Miller
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 5 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Pretty good class and prof. Curriculum is relevant, thought-provoking, and well-structured, but not unreasonably difficult for the most part. Grading is attendance and participation (30%), material response posts (30%), current events post (10%), and final research project (30%). My only frustration is that Britt has literally graded nothing yet...

I took her Envi Ed class (NRC 520) and was SHOCKED at how rudimentary the class was. I loathed coming to class bc of how surface level the material was (I study this stuff 4 my major). I got a C+ bc I didn't do the BS weekly nature journals. Not engaging or challenging whatsoever; ridiculous for a 500 lvl class. The final was so bad - Hot Mess

Class was very discussion-based. Read a couple of articles and papers each week and talked about them in class. I usually am not a fan of this teaching style, but hearing perspectives and thoughts from classmates and from Britt always helped me to piece together different themes and ideas from readings. Learned a lot, highly recommend!
Class was pretty interesting and easy. Not a lot of prep/effort from professor. Very discussion based. Grades are not posted throughout the semester and expectations are unclear.
Really good class. Prof was really passionate about our topics. She'll notice if you skip class though.

analysis.name: Cristina Vlas
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 7 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Prof Vlas is great! This class has a bad reputation in Isenberg but Cristina made it really fun and low stress. She makes sure you're well prepared for exams and gives great feedback for the capsim simulation. She will not let anyone fail!! Class was overall very easy and she is so nice and really cares about her students.

This class is a pain. However, Professor Vlas makes it a whole lot more manageable. We weren't graded on the CAPSIM which is a god send because that software hates fun. My class got moved to online midway through the semester because the Isenberg basement flooded lol. Overall, pretty easy course, workload kinda a pain at times. Make a good group.

Not a bad choice for an instructor for this course. The lecture portion of the class is pretty easy and very passable. The simulation section will make you lose your mind, but it is not her doing. She tried her best to help us along and with extra credit at the end, it was very easy to get an A.

You have class 15 minutes once a week. She expects you to have already read the slides. Talks about nothing during those 15 minutes. Lecture quizzes every week for the first half of semester. 10 minutes, 8 questions, never had enough time and they're hard questions. Similar with exams. Simulation makes absolutely no sense. No help outside of class.

This is a hard class, but mandatory. Ask her to zoom outside of class! She is so helpful and caring one on one. Do the extra credit and try your best to get high scores on at least 3 of the Simulation rounds. I can't stress enough - meet with her one on one!!!! I twill make all the difference in the virtual world. She is very sweet and caring.

analysis.name: Cole Reilly
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 21 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Yo this guy is genuinely the goat. Do NOT regret picking my man Cole Reilly, made my semester a breeze. Funny, chill, and a good lecturer. Inspirational man.

Cole is a funny guy who knows how to teach! All of his lectures are recorded, and the course material is neatly organized in Canvas/Piazza. His grading criteria make it very easy to do well in the class as long as you complete all of the work outside of class. He is accessible during and outside of class and will answer all of your questions.

He's the BEST professor ever! He's really casual (not strict), and is very understanding! He teaches content really well and we are typically ahead compared to others! We are mostly graded by the assignments (coding "projects") which r really easy! Labs aren't worth much & is easy group work, and quizzes are also easy cuz of the leniency w points!

Cole is hilarious and clearly cares about his student's success. Homeworks are 5ish question moodle "quizzes." 5-6 mini projects during the semester (sounds scary, but they're more akin to a traditional homework assignment in length and difficulty). Plenty of opportunities for assistance outside of class (office hours, TA's, class message board).

Cole is one of my favorite professors. The homework and exams are pretty easy. That being said, get ready to be seriously challenged with the coding projects, but he is always available to help. Very generous with extensions and will work with a student's unique circumstances as needed. Very caring teacher clearly passionate about the subject.

analysis.name: Crystal Paul
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, but ratings have been improving recently

analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 14 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Very kind, helpful and easily accessible professor who teaches concepts super well. The course itself was the hardest I've taken and required a lot of effort and study on my end, however, the professor did a fantastic job accommodating my learning throughout the course.

Professor Mcgregor is an amazing lecturer. His lectures are very clear and thorough. He makes sure everyone understands the material well.  On Piazza, he answers everyone's questions. He really is awesome and understanding of the students.

I have a lot of respect for Andrew because he actually cares very much about his students. He goes out of his way to answer questions in great detail and ensures you understand. The material can be somewhat abstract, but I don't see how anyone else can give better lectures. He is also a great guy, and structured the course very well. Pretty easy A

Andrew is the best prof/person I have ever met. He listens to students, answers EVERY question with details. His class is very organized too. He posts all lecture slides and solution to every homework and exam (even practice exam). Don't hesitate to take his class or have a conversation with him about compsci or math! He's always there for you.

Nice guy, very helpful as a teacher, understanding. DON'T MISS CLASS! EVER! If you go to class and pay attention, you'll do relatively well. Course material is boring and it can be hard to focus in class on what's happening. Tests make or break the class for you. Homeworks: very long, don't procrastinate on these! TAs/Teacher are helpful.

analysis.name: Andrew Donson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 60 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Prof. Donson is a really nice guys and wants his students to succeed. That being said, he is a very difficult grader. He does give multiple chances to improve on essays, and homework is relatively easy and counts for a good portion of the grade. In-class participation is very important to him as well.

Professor Donson is particularly arrogant, unhelpful, and generally annoying. This course was structured in a way that made it so that actually working on the biography was nearly unfeasible. He bombards everyone with peer reviews, three entire novels (all 200+ pages and due a week after being assigned), and countless other worthless assignments.

This is the worst class I've taken. Sample sentences consist of body shaming and domestic abuse in a way that is very triggering. Does not attend meetings with students that he sets. Grading is outrageously strict, and if you submit edits for additional credit, he'll forget to grade them. This is genuinely the worst classroom I've been in.

Warning: NOT A CLASS FOR THOSE WHO WANT AN EASY A.  Now that that's been said, this class should definitely be taken by anyone who wants to learn as much as possible about German history.  Professor Donson is super knowledgeable and helpful but he assigns a lot of reading and writing which makes up most of your grade.

DO NOT take this class if you're looking for an easy history gen-ed. He is very knowledgeable but assigns a lot of reading/questions every week. Sometimes readings don't match up with lectures and discussion sections are not helpful at all. The topic is very interesting but definitely not an easy class.

analysis.name: Sonja Drimmer
analysis.verdict: Good teaching but expect to put in the work
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 25 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Sonja Drimmer is the best professor I've had a UMASS. She takes her lectures and makes them incredibly engaging. Her excitement for the subject is apparent and makes classes that much more enjoyable. To be sure however, this class was in no way easy. Major work needs to be put in, especially for the papers.

Drimmer's teaching style is utterly exhausting, I was criticized for a paper being "too well written" (I received a C), she did not respond to my email sharing I had a death in the family, and her grading felt subjective.  I had to attend a 5 hour lecture on rugs to get a decent grade with extra credit.  Still traumatized (in grad school now.)

One of the best professors I've ever had. She is the most interesting, funny, charismatic professor I have ever had. She is so cool and kind, and makes class genuinely enjoyable. She fosters engagement effortlessly, making the classroom laugh often and so many kids always raise their hands, which I have found is rare. 100000/10, highly recommend!

Professor Drimmer is super kind and so beyond passionate about what she teaches and what she knows. She makes lectures fun and engaging (as someone who's never taken an art class). She is always very well prepared for class and always is open to questions and comments about art or things outside of it. Only 3 exams and two papers

She's a really good lecturer, enthusiastic about the material she teaches. She emphasizes the important stuff and makes really helpful reviews and sheets to follow along with. Discussion assignments were graded really easy. If you show up and take notes you'll do good.

analysis.name: Andrew Farrar
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 18 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Andy is the best professor I've ever had. He's not only a very funny and enjoyable lecturer who connects well with the class, but is also very efficient in his lecture material and facilitates useful discussions. He is straightfoward in his criteria and wants everyone to do well. Andy is love. Andy is life.

Andy is super personable and really tries to get to know his students and their interests. He will tailor lecture topics to student interests regularly. If you're trying to decide who to choose for CNS junior year writing, I really recommend him. He also schedules the class differently than the other professors, with less work around finals week.

Great guy, tries to be funny in class. Super interesting lectures and the exams are manageable. Dense information but definitely do-able. No homework! Only one group presentation. Overall fantastic class.

Andy meant well but was incredibly soft spoken and tried too hard to mix his humor into lecture content which became confusing. He often came off as rude and uncaring when contacted or approached with questions about the material. Wasted way too much time by calling attendance in our class, every single class, which had over 50 students in it.

Phenomenal professor, not only taught the most interesting class I've ever taken (Drugs and Behavior), but a very down to earth professor. The content in 535 is a bit dense, but he gives you every opportunity to succeed. Class is part lecture, part open discussion about fascinating aspects of pharmacology. Amazing class, amazing man, 10/10.

analysis.name: Lindsay  DuBois
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: Don't buy the textbook. Those who bought it quit reading it after the third chapter. Attendance is mandatory but she is kind about students who come in late. I had the class split into two 1.5hr sessions at 8am. Professor DuBois LOVES politics, so you mostly talk about current events. It's a super easy class, interesting at times.

Such a boring professor. Attendance is mandatory and she gives you scuff for not coming in when she doesn't do anything educational during class. She goes off topic and on random tangents all the time. She doesn't have structure for the class and her grading system is so confusing and never aligns with what she says.

Don't buy the book. Her class is flipped and you are responsible for learning all of the info outside of class. The assignments are poorly outlined. Graded on exit tickets, 3 papers, 3 discussions, 1 presentation, 2 group projects, and final exam. She just yaps through the whole class.

Her final is beyond frustrating as it is "Lecture-Based"; however, our class is completely unstructured. She will put a couple of slides up with words and then go on tangents, of random stories and irrelevant conversations.

Overall extremely poor professor. Multiple quizzes based on textbook alone with no lecture component (Lecture after the quiz, not before; very unhelpful!). Lack of actual teaching, overload of irrelevant personal stories. Being difficult to reach outside of class on top of rude (and late) email replies makes Lindsey a poor fit for this role.

analysis.name: Peter  Dunn
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 10 reviews, decent sample but could shift with more data

review_highlights.comment: Three papers, graded very easily. For two of them, I wrote a draft, edited it in under 30 minutes, and got above a 90%. Weekly homework for completion, very fun. Two weekly quizzes w/ 4 attempts. Final is an easy group project. Groups are assigned. Casual lecture style. Make sure to do all the little assignments, you can miss a few, but not many.

Not very difficult to get an A in this course, as there are no exams and the primary way to get points deducted is the essays, which he doesn't really give feedback on at all and also is pretty nitpicky about them, but it's fair. Lectures didn't feel engaging at all, but some of the topics were interesting. I'm an unrelated major, so maybe that's y

Lectures are kind of boring but oh well.  Regardless, he's an easily accessible professor, and the grading of assignments seems to be pretty lenient.  Just make sure to keep track of the graded online short quizzes and weekly activity assignments and you'll be fine.  There are 3 750-1000 word essays to be written but they were fairly doable.

I am really conflicted. This teacher is really nice and amazing but the content of the class is the most boring thing ever. The teacher is a little bit of a type A person but to the students benefit as the class is clearly structured. Despite him being a great person, the syllabus, slides, and lectures are painfully boring and uninteresting.

Peter is an advisor and head of the SustComm department. He's very interested in his students success and what he teaches. Only three shorter essays that were pretty easy to write. Helpful with course registration as well, if you can take this class and you are interested in SCD you should.

analysis.name: Duncan Irschick
analysis.verdict: Well liked with reasonable difficulty, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 33 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: In all my years of taking classes, its safe to say that his are among the best - a real gem - and last of all, his tests are super fair and a real treat to take - its definately an awesome class and one that i would take again anyday
Professor Irschick is a phenomenal lecturer. He is so engrained in the field of mammalian biology, I could not imagine anyone else teaching this course better.

One of the most clear and cogent professors in the department - whats really clear is that he REALLY cares about the students and is willing to spend a lot of time with you to ensure that you fully understand the material. Really an amazing professor and person.

Well all I can say is that its quite clear that this was an incredible and wonderful class with amazing clairty -the professor had remarkable vision and the ability to understand everyone and assign reasonable grades - take! take!

This class has 2 parts, the 2nd taught by Irschick. I liked the 1st half & grading was easy however it completely changed when he took over. He gives good feedback on summaries but grades harsh. Showing up is not enough to get a good participation grade from him. He didn't curve the exam (Gerson did). Overcomplicated everything & ruined my grade.

analysis.name: Joseph DuChene
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 8 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: His exams closely resemble exam review slides and TA review worksheets. Even if you skip lectures, attend the last class before each exam. Homework is graded based on effort and completion. The slides are clear and easy to understand. He is approachable, passionate about the subject, and does a great job explaining concepts!

The course material can be made rigorous if one follows the textbook (Bard Electrochemical Methods) but this class was very easy, only going over rudimentary concepts. Some of our exam questions were taken straight from the practice problems. The class is fairly pleasant to listen in on.
Professor DuChene is kind, and quick to the point. The course material is fairly simple, but I would still advise showing up to lecture as his slides do not give much information on their own.

unfortunately, it seems as though Joe is a professor who does not care too much at all about teaching. it may be possible that the department forced him into the role. he's a great guy and the class is easy to do well in but i didn't actually learn anything or gain any value from quant lecture. i shouldn't get an A in a class while learn nothing.

Joe is a great guy, but I did not learn anything from his class. All the exams are recycled from previous years, and all hw can be found online so it is easy to do well, however you learn nothing. The lab is a completely different story- one of the worst labs ive taken here. Stay away from this class if you can.

analysis.name: Marco Duarte
analysis.verdict: Most students had a tough time. Look into alternatives if you can
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 46 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Throughout my journey in university, I have never came across such a class and professor. Homeworks will receive terrible grades, regardless if you do them in office hours with the TA's. Awful experience in this class, DO NOT take this class with Duarte. Its clear that he's just doing this for the money and does not have passion for teaching.

Genuinely one of the hardest classes for a subject that is seemingly very simple in concept. The way everything was organized was the worst I've seen by far in any course I've taken. You're more likely to hit the lotto than getting good feedback on everything. Watch out for exams, because there WILL be things that were never mentioned.

Absolutely TERRIBLE class, assignments are graded with pure inconsistency and professor shows no understanding of the students' situations. TA graders are absolute nightmares and when brought to the professors attention, he does not do anything. Does not reply to 90% of emails.

grading is incomprehensible and practically random. be prepared to do every assignment 2-3 times.

you learn nothing and the whole class is graded based on his random bs criteria, huge waste of time, take prof. leonard instead

This class is just bad and the professor does not care about his students succeeding. Homework directions can be vague but grading is overly harsh. Just skip taking this guy and take professor leonard, anyone but professor duarte!

analysis.name: Dwanna Robertson
analysis.verdict: Mixed reviews. Student experiences vary quite a bit, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 4 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: I took Dee a while back. She was engaging and passionate about her work. However, she strikes me as a little self-centered, as she would only talk about indigenous people, and neglect other racial/ethnic minorities. She also rejected both myself and two others' LOR requests (too busy?) for grad school apps- again, somewhat selfish and unsupportive.

Dee was great! She may be a little intense about her ethnic background but she means well. She will tell it how it is and is very involved with her students. She will learn your name and who you are. Lots of easy writing and mostly free writes! Topics are inspiring and fun. Grades very fast with helpful comments and emails back quickly. Loved her!

Dee is a wonderful teacher! she really makes sense with her teaching...it is an easy a if you do all your work.  she even says its hard to fail this course.  she's very energetic and i looked forward coming to class even if it was 8am...i got an A! and it was so worth it. i highly recommend it! plus its 2 gen-eds
Dee is an awesome professor!She delves into issues that we see, but have never understood or knew they were they were there before. It's a great class!!

analysis.name: Rachael Dworsky
analysis.verdict: Below average reviews. Worth checking if this fits your learning style, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Only 6 reviews so far, take these numbers with a grain of salt

review_highlights.comment: This class is a Gen Ed for ALL students, yet Rachael grades as if each student is an English major. She is not understanding of attendance issues. It is extraordinarily difficult to predict what your final grade will be, as she uses a mixture of a check and number system, with no updates to where you stand.  Take this class with another teacher.

Rachael Dworsky is a sweet woman when she likes you, but definitely has a vicious side if you miss too many classes. Attendance is mandatory. I wasn't too crazy about her book selection but if you read you will do well. Pop quizzes, and a few essays. She gives you the option to choose the prompt you would like to answer in your essays. Fair class.

Worst class that I have taken. It appears as though she has difficulty understanding absences. She gives too much work and not enough time to complete the assignments, which is extremely annoying. Although she is not understanding...Rachael is a push over and you can easily by yourself more time, however.Good luck in not getting her angry.

TERRIBLE TEACHER! There is a lot of writing (to be expected), but it is complete and utter junk writing. She doesn't know what she is talking about and contradicts herself in her teaching. She has severe issues with her teaching style and does not seem to care if her students succeed at all. She is honestly the worst professor at umass.
this is by FAR with no doubt in my mind the worst teacher at all of umass. Take her class and then have the motivation to visit this website just to let people know.

analysis.name: Jacob Dyer-Spiegel
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, and ratings have been declining
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 40 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Jacob is an incredible professor who, despite not being an engineer, has figured out ways to get us (Engin majors from all fields) to describe our mindset, process, lens, and vision for the future.The activities and prompts were so interesting that I wanted to put more time into my writing and communicating. He turned writing into engineering!

This was my favorite course at UMass. I loved the interactive nature of everything we did and Jacob's constant encouragement. I found I learned a lot about my own engineering process through the course and the way Jacob focused on practice. Excellent professor, highly recommend taking extra time to do all of the work fully & extra credits!

Jacob's awesome! As an engineering major, I despise writing. However, I genuinely looked forward to each class, knowing I would be in an interactive and engaging environment. He provides excellent feedback and is extremely supportive, eager to help clarify any points of confusion. If you need to take Engin 351, take it with Jacob!

Really nice guy. He cares a lot about students and will take an interest in pretty much all of the essay topics even with limited technical knowledge. I normally hate writing, but he really made the process as manageable as possible. He also provides really detailed feedback on all of the major assignments you submit.

You can tell Jacob loves teaching. He brings a huge energy to the class, builds from everyone's interests & viewpoints, and always makes himself available for clarifications, examples, and feedback. What I liked most is the way the assignments get you practicing writing skills while giving space to be creative with our engineering interests.

analysis.name: Brion Dulac
analysis.verdict: Highly rated with a manageable workload, but ratings have been improving recently
analysis.confidence_detail: Based on 62 reviews, fairly reliable

review_highlights.comment: Brion is definitely a pretty funny guy but seems a little off his rocker. I've probably written over 100 pages on papers for this class, he's big on written assignments. Pretty easy grader though all you have to do is talk every now and then in the class and actually do the assignments. He's a little weird and goes on tangents but he's a great guy

Brion is a great teacher, and en even better man. He is often scatter brained but has the best intentions. The perfect combination of smart, funny, and sweet. His Honors 291A uses a lot of movies and inspired me to start towards my film certificate. He sometimes brings in food. His stories are always interesting. He cares about his students.

I'm really glad I toke this seminar with Dulac.He's a pretty cool guy especially when analyzing movies.There's not much to say but just do all your work with some effort and you should get a good grade especially since he doesn't give that much work compared to other H291A professors.Loved all the movies we watched.

If you're looking for that movie-quality zany college professor, Brion is it. The semester started out very reading-heavy, but mellowed out immensely about halfway through. Brion is always engaging and it's clear that he cares about his students. I would definitely recommend taking this course with him.

Literally the best professor you will ever have. The homework is a ton, but very manageable if you email him for an extention. The papers he has you write are very reflective on yourself and on the topics in class. He is very caring and all-in-all the best person to meet in your life.
